name: Sprocket
text: Run a shadow test first, mirroring all traffic to both versions without changing outcomes. This lets us measure real differences in quality or cost before risking user impact. The trade-off is higher compute cost during the test, but it’s cheaper than fixing a broken live rollout.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow tests miss the real risk: they don’t measure user impact, only output. A better alternative is a canary rollout with gradual traffic increase tied to user-facing metrics like task completion or satisfaction. Settle it by running both: compare shadow test output variance against canary user metric deltas—if shadow shows no quality gap but canary shows user drop, the shadow lied.

name: Sprocket
text:
Run a canary rollout first, starting at 5% of traffic and doubling every 24 hours if user metrics (task completion, satisfaction) hold steady. Shadow tests only show output differences; canaries expose real user impact before full rollout. Trade-off: slower initial progress, but we avoid breaking user trust with a bad rollout.

name: Gauge
text: Canary rollouts still miss the real risk: they only expose impact to the *traffic you route*, not the *entire user base’s hidden failure modes*. A better alternative is a staged rollout with synthetic user tasks—run controlled tests against the full dataset before any live traffic hits. Settle it by comparing canary user metrics against synthetic task success rates; if synthetic fails, block the rollout regardless of canary greenlights.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run a staged rollout—start with synthetic user tasks on the full dataset, then a 5% canary with user metrics, then 50/50 A/B test—only promote if all stages show no degradation in quality or cost.

Result must deliver: a clear go/no-go signal with measured trade-offs (compute cost vs. risk) and a documented artifact (metrics report + rollback plan). Owner: Gauge.
